Documentation.name: SPEM
Documentation.notes: Software and systems process engineering using the SPEM 2.0 metamodel.

Stereotype.name: SPEM_Activity
Stereotype.notes: <font color="#008080">An Activity is a Work Breakdown Element and Work Definition that defines basic units of work within a Process as well as a Process itself. </font>

Stereotype.name: SPEM_Association
Stereotype.notes: Use for SPEM customized use connector.

Stereotype.name: SPEM_BreakdownElement
Stereotype.notes: <font color="#008080">Breakdown Element is an abstract generalization for any type of Process Element that is part of a breakdown structure. It defines a set of properties available to all of its specializations. Any of its concrete subclasses can be 'placed inside' an Activity (via the nested Breakdown Element association) to become part of a breakdown of Activities as well as the Activities namespace. </font>

Stereotype.name: SPEM_Category
Stereotype.notes: <font color="#008080">A Category is a Describable Element used to categorize, i.e., group any number of Describable Elements of any subtype based on user-defined criteria. </font>

Stereotype.name: SPEM_CompositeRole
Stereotype.notes: <font color="#008080">A Composite Role is a grouping of Role Definitions that can be used in an Activity or Process to reduce the number of Roles defined in Method Content. </font>

Stereotype.name: SPEM_DescribableElement
Stereotype.notes: <font color="#008080">Describable Element is an Extensible Element that represents an abstract generalization for all elements in SPEM 2.0 that can be documented with textual descriptions. Examples for Describable Elements are Roles or Work Products, which have descriptive text associated that textually define the element as well as providing guidance on how to use it. </font>

Stereotype.name: SPEM_ExtensibleElement
Stereotype.notes: <font color="#008080">Extensible Element is an abstract generalization that represents any SPEM 2.0 class for which it is possible to assign a Kind to its instances expressing a user-defined qualification. </font>

Stereotype.name: SPEM_Guidance
Stereotype.notes: <font color="#008080">Guidance is a Describable Element that provides additional information related to Describable Elements. </font>

Stereotype.name: SPEM_MethodContentElement
Stereotype.notes: <font color="#008080">Method Content Element is an abstract Describable Element that represents an abstract generalization for all Method Content Elements in SPEM 2.0. </font>

Stereotype.name: SPEM_MethodContentPackage
Stereotype.notes: <font color="#008080">A Method Content Package is a Method Content Packageable Element and Package that contains Method Content Elements only. Examples for Method Content Element are Work Product Definition, Task Definition, Role Definition, etc. </font>

Stereotype.name: SPEM_Metric
Stereotype.notes: A Metric is a special Describable Element that contains one or more constraints that provide measurements for any Describable Element.

Stereotype.name: SPEM_Milestone
Stereotype.notes: <font color="#008080">A Milestone describes a significant event in a development project, such as a major decision, completion of a deliverable, or meeting of a major dependency (like completion of a project phase). </font>

Stereotype.name: SPEM_ParameterInOut
Stereotype.notes: <font color="#008080">A Work Definition Parameter instance with this direction value represents an input and output.</font>

Stereotype.name: SPEM_Performer
Stereotype.notes: <font color="#008080">Typical examples for Kinds of Process Performers would be Primary Performer, Additional Performer, Assisting Performer, Supervising Performer, Consulted Performer, etc. </font>

Stereotype.name: SPEM_ProcessElement
Stereotype.notes: <font color="#008080">A Process Element is any element that is part of a Process. </font>

Stereotype.name: SPEM_Qualification
Stereotype.notes: <font color="#008080">A Qualification documents one specific skill or competency that is used to model and represent the qualifications provided by instances of a Role Definition and/or the qualifications required for the performance of a Task. </font>

Stereotype.name: SPEM_ResponsibilityAssignment
Stereotype.notes: <font color="#008080">The Process Responsibility Assignment links Role Uses to Work Product Uses indicating that the Role Use has a responsibility relationship with the Work Product Use. </font>

Stereotype.name: SPEM_RoleDefinition
Stereotype.notes: <font color="#008080">A Role Definition is a Method Content Element that defines a set of related skills, competencies, and responsibilities. </font>

Stereotype.name: SPEM_RoleUse
Stereotype.notes: <font color="#008080">A Role Use is a special Breakdown Element that either represents a performer of an Activity or a participant of the Activity. </font>

Stereotype.name: SPEM_Section
Stereotype.notes: <font color="#008080">A Section is a special Class that represents a structural subsection of a Content Description's mainDescription attribute. </font>

Stereotype.name: SPEM_Step
Stereotype.notes: <font color="#008080">A Step is a Section and Work Definition that is used to organize a Task Definition's Content Description into parts or subunits of work. </font>

Stereotype.name: SPEM_TaskDefinition
Stereotype.notes: <font color="#008080">A Task Definition is a Method Content Element and a Work Definition that defines work being performed by Roles Definition instances. </font>

Stereotype.name: SPEM_ToolDefinition
Stereotype.notes: <font color="#008080">A Tool Definition is a special Method Content Element that can be used to specify a tool's participation in a Task Definition. </font>

Stereotype.name: SPEM_WorkBreakdownElement
Stereotype.notes: <font color="#008080">Work Breakdown Element represents a work-specific breakdown element to be used in a work breakdown structure. </font>

Stereotype.name: SPEM_WorkDefinition
Stereotype.notes: <font color="#008080">Work Definition is an abstract Classifier that generalizes all definitions of work within SPEM 2.0. Work Definition defines some default associations to Work Definition Parameter and Constraint. </font>

Stereotype.name: SPEM_WorkProductUse
Stereotype.notes: <font color="#008080">A Work Product Use represents an activity-specific occurrence of a Work Product input/output type or an Activity participant. </font>

Stereotype.name: SPEM_WorkSequence
Stereotype.notes: <font color="#008080">The Work Sequence class defines predecessor and successor relations among Work Breakdown Elements. </font>
